sections.title: A verb you know, one more use for it
sections.content: You already know tervez with a plain object — Vasárnap tervezünk egy kirándulást ("We're planning a hike on Sunday"). tervez can also take a bare infinitive directly, exactly like elkezd already does: Mit tervezel csinálni? ("What are you planning to do?"). Whatever comes after tervez as an infinitive names the action you're actively planning, not just an object you're arranging.

items.english: What are you planning to do tonight?
I'm planning to help Ildikó this weekend.

items.spanish: Károly és Petra terveznek utazni nyáron.
items.english: Károly and Petra are planning to travel in the summer.

sections.content: tervez + infinitive works the same shape as tervez + noun — just conjugate tervez for the person, and let whatever follows (object or infinitive) stay exactly as it is.
